input.quote: Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only for-cause, insolvency and Customer-specific cause triggers (9.1–9.3), plus a force-majeure exit in 27.3; there is no termination-for-convenience right for either party. Under a three-year term (8.1) the absence of a Customer convenience right is a deviation, so we have inserted a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and confirmed Vendor has none. Favourably, no Vendor convenience right exists.

input.quote: Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
input.rationale: The 180-day non-renewal notice window exceeds even the walk-away threshold of 90 days and fails the fallback of 60 days; we have shortened it to 30 days. The 12-month renewal term and the CPI/3% uplift cap with 90 days' notice in 8.3 are favourable and unchanged.

input.quote: This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
input.rationale: Meets our preferred position: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County, and no arbitration (foreign or otherwise). The pre-suit executive escalation in 28.3 expressly preserves urgent relief and limitations filings, so it is not an obstacle.
